title: Boolean disagreement and relative Hamming distance
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $f,g:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be Boolean-valued functions. The squared uniform $2$-norm of the difference between their real-valued sign representations equals four times their relative Hamming distance, namely four times the number of inputs on which they disagree divided by $2^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $f,g$ are functions from the Boolean cube to the signs $\{-1,1\}$
